name: Dip bars
lead: Dip bars (parallel bars or dip stations) are two horizontal handles at roughly hip height or higher on which the user supports their bodyweight on straight arms and lowers and raises the body. They come as freestanding stands, wall-mounted bars, power-rack attachments or small portable units.

The movement trains the lower chest, front shoulders and triceps and, when weighted, can be progressed for years. It is popular as a bodyweight upper-body builder that complements pull-ups for balanced pressing and pulling.

paras: Pressing the body away from the handles loads the pectorals, triceps and anterior deltoids, and leaning the torso forward shifts more work to the chest. As a bodyweight exercise it can be progressed with added weight belts or vests, slower reps and pauses, in line with general resistance-training principles.

Deep dips place the shoulder in extension and internal rotation, which is a known irritant for people with shoulder problems, and elbow tendon strain is also reported. Unstable or narrow cheap stands are a safety issue. There is little direct research on dips versus alternatives, so the claim that they are an excellent chest builder rests on general resistance-training evidence and anatomy rather than dip-specific trials.
